NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday claimed that Meta had restricted his Instagram account in India without providing any explanation. He alleged that repeated attempts to seek clarification from the company's India office had gone unanswered.In a post on X, Kejriwal tagged Meta and Meta India, saying his account had become unavailable to users in India."Hi @Meta @metaindia Why have you restricted my account? Verbal enquiries at your India office revealed that my account has been restricted in India and is unavailable in India. Why? Noone in your office is giving any reasons. Noone is suggesting how restrictions can be removed. All emails written have elicited no response other than routine acknowledgement. Thats pretty bad service. Don’t bow down to our Prime Minister so much. Else he will allow u to run only his own account in India," he said.Kejriwal alleged that officials at Meta's India office informed him verbally about the restriction but did not disclose the reason behind the action or explain how it could be reversed. He also claimed that emails sent to the company had received only routine acknowledgements.The AAP leader further accused Meta of "bowing down" to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging political bias in the platform's actions.Kejriwal's allegation comes a day after Meta apologised to the government over the erroneous removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook. The company attributed the incident to a technical error, with Meta's chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan saying he had apologised to Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on behalf of the company.The apology followed a parliamentary panel's warning that Meta could risk losing its intermediary "safe harbour" protection if it failed to explain the removal of the Prime Minister's video. During discussions with the government, Meta also acknowledged lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfakes and paid content amplification, while assuring authorities that corrective measures would be implemented.Meta has not yet publicly responded to Kejriwal's latest claims regarding the alleged restriction of his Instagram account.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claims that Meta had restricted his Instagram account in India. He alleged that repeated attempts to seek clarification from the company's India office had gone unanswered. Kejriwal's allegation comes a day after Meta apologised to the government over the erroneous removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook.

Article Title: Air India turbulence lasted 'four to five minutes'; some passengers still in hospital
Article Text:
Some passengers still in hospital

NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.Addressing the media, Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody."In terms of why the incident has happened, we have immediately alerted the DGCA to thoroughly investigate the situation. The moment the plane was landed, it was put in a separate hangar. The data recorder, the voice recorder, everything is in the possession of DGCA. They will thoroughly investigate how and why this incident happened. Only when we have the facts in front of us, we are going to make it public," he said.The minister said medical teams attended to passengers and crew immediately after the flight landed in Delhi."The moment the flight landed in Delhi, the medical assistance team immediately attended to them. All first aid and medical assistance that needed to be provided was done at the airport itself. There were some passengers and crew members who were observed to need more medical assistance, they were shifted to Medanta Hospital and also Fortis Hospital," Naidu added.He said seven passengers admitted to Medanta Hospital on Monday were discharged after undergoing medical examinations."Spinal Injuries Centre, Fortis Centre - two passsengers were admitted yesterday. They both were also discharged but four crew members were admitted in Fortis where I also personally visited along with Ministry Team and DGCA Team. We interacted with crew members also. They have been very brave, even after that incident happened for 5 minutes and they were prone to certain injuries, the plane had to travel for 1 more hour. Even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance that was required. So, it was very brave of the women, the crew members who were on the flight," he said.The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday, was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members. Following the turbulence, 13 passengers and four crew members sustained injuries and were taken to hospitals for medical evaluation.According to Air India, as of 6:50 pm, five passengers had been discharged, while the remaining injured continued to receive treatment and care.An Air India spokesperson said on Tuesday, "Earlier today, Air India flight AI2379 operating from Phuket to Delhi experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise. After the momentary event, the aircraft continued normally and landed safely in Delhi at 11:07 hrs IST."The DGCA is now investigating the incident to determine the cause of the severe midair turbulence.
Article Summary: Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes" At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing.

Article Title: Centre deploys national team as Chandipura outbreak probe intensifies
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: With 35 laboratory-confirmed Chandipura virus infections and 22 deaths among 184 suspected cases reported in children under 15 across Gujarat this monsoon, and the virus also affecting children from neighbouring Rajasthan, the Centre on Wednesday deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to strengthen outbreak investigations and accelerate scientific efforts to contain the disease.Chandipura virus, a sandfly-borne virus that primarily affects children, can rapidly progress from fever to acute encephalitis syndrome (AES), a severe brain infection. While sandflies are the established vector, scientists are investigating whether mosquitoes, ticks or mites may also be involved in the current outbreak.The virus is not new to India. First identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra in 1965, it has caused periodic outbreaks of acute encephalitis among children in states such as Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, particularly during the monsoon.The multidisciplinary team, comprising experts from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), will support state authorities in outbreak investigation, epidemiological assessment, laboratory coordination, clinical management and vector surveillance. The NCDC's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre has also been activated to coordinate the response.Rajasthan has stepped up surveillance after children from the state, including a two-year-old girl, tested positive for Chandipura virus while undergoing treatment in Gujarat. The cross-border cases prompted the Centre to include Rajasthan in its coordinated response.The deployment comes amid one of the country's most extensive scientific investigations into Chandipura virus in recent years, involving multiple ICMR institutes, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC). Scientists are trying to answer key questions about the virus's transmission, clinical spectrum and evolution while generating evidence to guide public health measures.Surveillance has been intensified among patients with acute febrile illness (AFI) and acute encephalitis syndrome, while community serosurveys are underway to estimate the extent of asymptomatic infections. Researchers are also analysing samples from sandflies, mosquitoes, ticks and mites to identify the vector responsible for the current outbreak.At the same time, blood and milk samples from cattle, buffaloes and goats are being tested to determine whether domestic animals could act as virus reservoirs.Around 70 animal blood samples have been collected so far and are being analysed for Chandipura virus and other relevant pathogens.Scientists are also carrying out whole-genome sequencing of virus samples to determine whether the circulating strain has undergone genetic changes. Officials said findings from the investigation, together with data generated through India's hospital-based Acute Encephalitis Syndrome surveillance network, will strengthen outbreak detection, improve understanding of the disease and support evidence-based public health interventions.
Article Summary: Chandipura virus, a sandfly-borne virus that primarily affects children, can rapidly progress from fever to acute encephalitis syndrome. 22 deaths among 184 suspected cases reported in children under 15 across Gujarat this monsoon. The virus also affecting children from neighbouring Rajasthan.

Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road.

Article Title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
Article Text:
The government says that the company admits lapses on child porn, deepfakes

Officials told Meta it could lose safe harbour status

NEW DELHI: Amid mounting scrutiny, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has apologised to the government for Facebook taking down PM Modi’s video, and the social media giant’s lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfake content and errors in operating its platforms, government officials said. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content, the officials added.Meta blamed technical glitches for Modi’s video being taken down, in which he had reached out to student protesters.“I apologised to the minister (Ashwini Vaishnaw) on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post,” Meta’s chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan said in a statement. Government officials said Zuckerberg’s apology was communicated through Kaplan.The apology came hours after Zuckerberg was given a three-day ultimatum by a parliamentary standing committee headed by BJP’s Nishikant Dubey on Wednesday to either apologise for taking down PM Modi’s video or lose the ‘safe harbour’ that protects Meta from any liability for the content posted on its platforms.The social media giant acknowledged during discussions with the government that significant sums had been paid for boosting certain categories of content and accepted that paid promotion had resulted in illegal content being amplified for specific audiences, officials said.The company expressed regret over the lapses and admitted mistakes in the way the platform had been operating, officials added.The meeting happened against the backdrop of widespread indignation in BJP and government quarters that Facebook facilitated algorithmic manipulation to fan discontent against the government over paper leaks and promote content, including a barrage of vile reels targeting the PM. Meta representatives will be summoned again, officials said, without disclosing the purpose or scope of the next meeting.Meta apologised for the shortcomings and assured authorities that corrective steps would be taken.Authorities also conveyed to Meta that it could not automatically claim protection available to intermediaries under Indian law if it actively selected who received content through algorithmic amplification or paid promotion. The company was told that such conduct could place it outside the definition of an intermediary, rendering it vulnerable to action by authorities and lawsuits by individuals.The government also sought details of safeguards to prevent the dissemination of CSAM, deepfakes and other harmful material. Officials said Meta accepted that illegal content had been promoted and acknowledged shortcomings in its systems.The government, meanwhile, is examining global regulatory approaches to children’s online safety as part of a broader review of its policy and legal framework. International models for protecting children online are being studied to assess whether additional safeguards or legislative changes are required as digital platforms come under increasing scrutiny over harmful and illegal content, it said in a statement.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg has apologised to the government for Facebook taking down PM Modi’s video. The social media giant also admitted lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and deepfake content. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content.

Article Title: Decide on raising retirement age of judges by Sept 2: SC to states
Article Text:
The Supreme Court requested high courts to pass appropriate full-court resolutions in favour of increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers from 60 to 62 years

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Attempting to bring judicial officers’ retirement age on a par with that for HC judges, the Supreme Court on Wednesday asked states to decide by Sept 2 on increasing the superannuation age of trial court judges from 60 to 62 years while brushing aside pleas of financial constraints and the disparity it would create vis-a-vis government employees.In the early 1990s, the Supreme Court had increased through a judgment the retirement age of judicial officers across India from 58 to 60 years. This time, however, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that instead of a judicial ruling, it would be better if state governments made the decision on their own. The strength of trial court judges has doubled since 1992, from around 10,000 to over 20,000 at present. The number of HC judges has increased from 568 in 1992 to 1,114 now.A few states have increased the age of retirement for judicial officers from 60 to 61, akin to similar benefits for government employees. Some states argued that increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers to 62 years would create disparity and cause discontent among government employees, who too would demand identical benefits, entailing a huge financial burden for the government.But the bench rejected both these objections. It said that when a judicial officer retires, the government pays them a lump-sum amount and pension, which is more than half of their last-drawn salary. On filling the vacancy, the government pays a salary to the new appointee. Retaining experienced and seasoned judicial officers would be financially beneficial for the state and judiciary, it said.Rejecting the argument of parity with government employees, the CJI-led bench said judicial officers are appointed by the government under a constitutional scheme and hence form a class separate from that of government employees. “Both the reasons given by states are untenable. But we are of the opinion that the issue can be resolved amicably by administrative decisions of states,” the bench said.Asking advocates general of states to persuade their respective governments, the bench said, “States must revisit the issue of enhancing the retirement age of judicial officers irrespective of the present retirement age of government employees.”The Supreme Court requested high courts to strengthen the hands of state governments on the issue by passing appropriate full-court resolutions in favour of increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers from 60 to 62 years.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court asked states to decide by Sept 2 on increasing the superannuation age of trial court judges from 60 to 62 years. The Supreme Court had increased through a judgment the retirement age of judicial officers across India from 58 to 60 years in the early 1990s.

Article Title: Rijiju reaches out to Rahul on delimitation bill
Article Text:
Speculation grew that the government may revive the Constitution amendment bill that was defeated in the last session

NEW DELHI: The government on Wednesday revived its bid to secure Parliament’s nod for its ambitious delimitation legislation that proposes to raise Lok Sabha’s strength by over 50% and implement one-third reservation for women from 2029, and appeared keen to press ahead despite LoP Rahul Gandhi rejecting its outreach for support.Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju raised the issue during his nearly 50-minute meeting with Rahul, who reiterated the Opposition’s stand that the proposed move would allow the government to redraw Lok Sabha constituencies to the NDA’s advantage in the next elections.The meeting was part of the government’s outreach to break the Parliament impasse, which has seen little business due to protests over multiple issues. However, speculation grew that the government may revive the Constitution amendment bill that was defeated in the last session.The timing remains uncertain. While a government functionary said it could be introduced before Aug 13, when the session is scheduled to end, official sources indicated Parliament may be reconvened after Aug 15 instead of being prorogued.There are indications that the government will push the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Bill, criticised by Opposition parties, NGOs, Muslim organisations and church bodies.On Tuesday, several of these groups sought the support of US lawmaker Riley Moore.At Wednesday’s meeting, Rahul Gandhi was accompanied by AICC general secretary KC Venugopal and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. According to sources, Congress conveyed that the rationale behind both the legislations was flawed.Venugopal said, “Minister Kiren Rijiju came to discuss delimitation and asked whether the Opposition’s stand had changed. We said we stick to the stand we took in the budget session... It has not changed.”Asked about the FCRA amendment bill, Venugopal said, “We will not allow the government to pass such a draconian bill.”On speculation that Rijiju hinted at a special session for the delimitation bill, Congress sources said he made no such suggestion. During the previous session too, the government had reconvened Parliament for three days after the scheduled end by not proroguing it. Having suffered the embarrassment of the earlier bill being defeated after securing only 298 votes against the required 352, the government appears to have strengthened its numbers for another attempt.Its position has improved since then as 26 Opposition MPs from Mamata Banerjee-led TMC and Sena UBT have joined the NDA, while DMK’s ties with Congress have deteriorated after the latter aligned with Vijay-led TVK in Tamil Nadu.The possibility of DMK, which had strongly opposed the bill earlier, extending support has increased after the party indicated it could back the proposal if southern states’ interests are protected. To allay such concerns, home minister Amit Shah had assured LS during the earlier debate that every state’s seats would increase by 50%, preserving their existing share in the House.There is a view that the government may incorporate the home minister’s assurance into the bill to win over parties such as DMK. NCP (SP) has also said a proposal guaranteeing the same increase in seats for every state should not pose a problem.
Article Summary: The government appears keen to press ahead despite LoP Rahul Gandhi rejecting its outreach for support. Speculation grew that the government may revive the Constitution amendment bill that was defeated in the last session. There are indications the government will push the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Bill.

Article Title: Government hits out at Pakistan’s malicious propaganda against India
Article Text:
MEA said the constitutional changes made on August 5, 2019, are entirely an internal matter of India

NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan for the so-called Youm-e-Istehsal (Day of Exploitation), which it observes on August 5, saying Pakistan’s desperate attempts to peddle falsehoods are intended solely to deflect international attention from its own dismal human rights record and its status as the global epicentre of terrorism.In a statement, ministry of external affairs (MEA) said the constitutional changes made on August 5, 2019, are entirely an internal matter of India and that these decisions had brought unprecedented socio-economic development, good governance, and democratic empowerment to the people of the region.On August 5, 2019, the government revoked the special status of J&K granted under Article 370 and bifurcated the state into UTs of J&K and Ladakh.“India categorically rejects the political absurdity and futile attempts by Pakistan to observe the so-called Youm-e-Istehsal to spread malicious propaganda against India. Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are, have always been, and shall forever remain an integral and inalienable part of India,” said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, adding that Pakistan has no locus standi to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India.The international community is currently witnessing the brutal suppression of fundamental rights in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), said the official.“Recent weeks have seen Pakistani security forces resort to lethal violence, targeted killings, and draconian bans to silence peaceful civil rights protests led by the local populace. Such state-sponsored violence against unarmed civilians exposes the profound hypocrisy of the Pakistani establishment,” he said.“Instead of engaging in predictable diplomatic theatre, Pakistan would be well-advised to stop the bloodshed in PoJK, take credible, verifiable, and irreversible action against terror networks operating from its soil, and immediately vacate all Indian territories under its illegal and forcible occupation. The world is not fooled by these orchestrated spectacles,” added the official.
Article Summary: India slams Pakistan for the so-called Youm-e-Istehsal (Day of Exploitation) It says Pakistan’s desperate attempts to peddle falsehoods are intended solely to deflect international attention from its own dismal human rights record.

Article Title: ‘Criminal cases can’t have lifespan of turtle’: Supreme Court on activist’s trial delay
Article Text:
Supreme Court of India

NEW DELHI: “Lifespan of a criminal trial cannot be that of a turtle,” SC said Wednesday, taking exception to the over-three-year-long trial of an activist of the outlawed Popular Front of India (PFI) facing charges that entail a maximum five-year jail term, with no prospect of its early end because of 700 prosecution witnesses lined up against him.Petitioner Shahid Khan , who was arrested on Sept 22, 2022, has appealed against a Karnataka HC order rejecting his bail plea. He is accused of helping raise funds for PFI between 2011 and 2019, and helping teams of the banned outfit which were planning attacks in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala in retaliation against the enactment of Citizenship (Amendment) Act, move to prepare a National Register of Citizens, and court judgments relating to hijab and Babri demolition.His counsel said the activities for which Shahid was arrested could not be classified as UAPA offences as his association with PFI predated the ban imposed on the outfit.He also argued the allegations against the appellant that he was providing training and raising funds for alleged terror activities carried a punishment of up to five years. “There is no chance of early completion of trial. Though he has a good chance of getting acquitted, he has already spent more than half of the sentence that would have been awarded to him on conviction,” the counsel said. Turning to Karnataka counsel, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Don’t make a mockery of the trial. ”
Article Summary: Shahid Khan is an activist of the outlawed Popular Front of India (PFI) facing charges that entail a maximum five-year jail term. He is accused of helping raise funds for PFI between 2011 and 2019, and helping teams of the banned outfit which were planning attacks.

Article Title: 'Apologised to minister': Meta official on PM Modi post removal; Zuckerberg sorry for deepfakes

NEW DELHI: Meta officials apologised to the IT minister for removing PM Modi's video while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg also reportedly sent his apologies to the central government on Wednesday for CSAM (child sexual abuse material), deepfake content, and errors in operating the platform."I apologised to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post," said Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer at Meta, as quoted by ANI. Kaplan, with his team, had met Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Wednesday.The government flagged the removal of content posted by verified accounts belonging to prominent personalities after a video of PM Modi was briefly removed from Facebook. The video, in which PM Modi addressed students and Gen Z on examination controversies and action against paper leaks, was removed from Facebook for around five to six hours before being restored.Separately, the IT also giant admitted that they were paid a "lot of money" for boosting certain type of content to "specific audiences", as per PTI sources. The sources also said that Meta was told that its eligibility for safe-harbour protection under the IT Act could be questioned, as its platforms actively select and distribute content to users rather than merely hosting third-party content. Under Section 79, safe-harbour protection is subject to conditions on how an intermediary handles and distributes such content.The development comes as senior Meta executives met government officials to discuss compliance with Indian laws, content moderation, child sexual CSAM and safeguards around AI-generated content.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, the company's head of public policy, met government officials on Wednesday and are set to meet again on Thursday.Krishnan said the government wants Meta to explain what measures it has taken to tackle CSAM on its platforms and how effectively it is monitoring synthetically generated content. “We want to ensure that compliance happens. There are a range of issues,” Krishnan said.He added that the government wants to understand the measures being taken to address CSAM and the extent to which AI-generated content is being monitored.The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Electronics and Information Technology had taken a “very serious” view of the incident and warned that Meta could lose its safe-harbour protection under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act if Zuckerberg failed to apologise within three days last week.Krishnan said such takedowns should be backed by stronger safeguards, particularly when they involve accounts of prominent public figures.
Article Summary: Meta officials apologised to the IT minister for removing PM Modi's video. Article Title: Air India turbulence scare: After the drop, the trauma lingers
Article Text:
Doctors say the physical and mental toll can last for months (Photo: ANI).

NEW DELHI: The Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi that suddenly dropped nearly 300 feet after encountering severe turbulence on Tuesday has once again highlighted that the impact of such incidents extends well beyond visible injuries. While at least 14 passengers and cabin crew members were injured and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation, doctors say the physical and psychological consequences of severe turbulence can linger for days, weeks or even months.Psychiatrists warn that even passengers who escape with minor or no physical injuries may develop significant psychological distress. "The sudden perception of imminent danger, combined with the loss of control and visible panic, can activate the body's survival response," said Dr Rajesh Sagar, professor in the Department of Psychiatry at AIIMS.Dr Sagar said that passengers may experience persistent fear, anxiety, sleep disturbances, intrusive memories and heightened alertness after the incident. In some cases, the experience can trigger Acute Stress Disorder (ASD) within days, which may progress to Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) if symptoms persist beyond a month."The psychological impact should not be underestimated simply because there are no major physical injuries," Dr Sagar said.He advised passengers to seek help if they continue to experience nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance of flying or emotional distress. Early psychological support based on the principles of Psychological First Aid can reduce the risk of long-term trauma, he added.Doctors also cautioned against dismissing apparently minor physical injuries sustained during turbulence. Dr (Maj.) Mukesh Garg, Director of Orthopaedics, Arthroscopy and Sports Injury at Sarvodaya Hospital, said passengers thrown against seats, overhead bins or cabin interiors may sustain bruises, ligament injuries, fractures or injuries to the neck and spine."Not all injuries become obvious immediately," he said. "Soft tissue injuries, ligament tears and mild concussions may take several hours to become apparent. Pain, swelling and stiffness often worsen over the next 24 to 48 hours."He advised anyone who suffered a blow to the head, neck or back to undergo medical evaluation even if symptoms initially appear mild. Warning signs requiring immediate medical attention include severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, dizziness, confusion, blurred vision, weakness or numbness of the limbs, difficulty walking, severe neck pain and loss of bladder or bowel control.Experts also recommend that passengers who develop a fear of flying after severe turbulence gradually rebuild confidence through counselling, breathing exercises and relaxation techniques. Starting with shorter flights, travelling with a trusted companion and keeping the seatbelt fastened throughout the journey can also help restore a sense of safety and control.
Article Summary: Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi suddenly dropped nearly 300 feet after severe turbulence on Tuesday. At least 14 passengers and cabin crew members were injured and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation has launched an investigation. Doctors say the physical and psychological consequences of severe turbulence can linger for days, weeks or even months.

NEW DELHI: The government is working to have the country’s Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System or NaVIC up and running again as it plans to launch four satellites in the near future.“NVS-03 is ready for launch after incorporation of all corrective measures arising from the NVS-02 anomaly. It will be followed by the launch of NVS-04 and NVS-05. One more satellite is planned thereafter to complete the seven-satellite NavIC base layer constellation,” space minister Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday.He, however, did not mention the timeline for these launches.Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said, “Necessary corrective measures have been incorporated and successfully implemented and tested in CMS-03 satellite. But for the NaVIC system to be operational effectively, at least four satellites with operational atomic clocks are required. So, NavIC is no longer providing standalone positioning services.In March this year, the last atomic clock on board Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning, paralysing NavIC.The first-generation satellites for NavIC were launched between 2013 and 2018. However, the constellation of satellites soon began to face issues, with the atomic clocks on board several IRNSS series satellites repeatedly malfunctioning.The NVS series represents the second-generation satellites for NavIC. While Isro successfully placed NVS-01 in the desired orbit in 2023, the 2025 launch of NVS-02 failed. This has delayed the launch of NVS-03, NVS-04 and NVS-05.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has threatened a nationwide strike if the Maharashtra government does not withdraw its recent decision permitting registration of BHMS graduates (Homepathy) who have completed the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC).In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the government’s August 3 Government Resolution (GR) “illegal” and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health.The controversy centres on the state’s decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls “dual medical council registration.”“The CCMP course has not been approved by the erstwhile Medical Council of India (MCI), the National Medical Commission (NMC), or the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH). Such a course cannot be considered valid and should be discontinued immediately,” the association said in its representation.The doctors’ body also argued that allowing practitioners to hold registrations under two different medical councils is unprecedented in India and could mislead patients regarding a doctor’s qualifications and scope of practice.The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court in a petition challenging amendments to the Maharashtra Medical Council Act. It said the government should not proceed with registrations while the matter remains sub judice.Questioning the state’s justification of addressing rural doctor shortages, the association claimed the circumstances have changed significantly since similar provisions were introduced over a decade ago.“The Maharashtra government has already done away with the compulsory rural bond system for MBBS graduates because of the non-availability of vacant posts, indicating that there is no longer a shortage of qualified allopathic doctors,” the letter stated.The association also said equating MBBS graduates, who undergo years of full-time medical education, with CCMP-trained practitioners who complete a part-time course would be unfair to students pursuing modern medicine.Citing the Supreme Court’s landmark judgment in Poonam Verma vs Ashwin Patel (1996), the IMA reiterated that practitioners registered in one recognised system of medicine cannot prescribe medicines or practise another system without recognised qualifications and valid registration in that system.The IMA warned that if the GR is not withdrawn and the CCMP course is not discontinued, it will call for a nationwide strike involving doctors of modern medicine, including medical students, resident doctors and interns across the country.Copies of the representation have also been sent to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Union Health Minister and the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission.

Article Title: Beyond Donations: How CSR Is Rewriting India’s Education Story
Article Text:
India has largely succeeded in getting children into school.

For years, corporate social responsibility (CSR) in education was measured by the number of classrooms built, computers donated, or scholarships awarded. Today, that metric is changing. As India’s education system moves beyond expanding access towards improving learning outcomes, companies are increasingly investing in programmes that strengthen govt schools, train teachers, improve employability and build long-term partnerships with public institutions.The shift comes at a critical moment. India has largely succeeded in getting children into school. According to UDISE+ 2024-25, the country has 14.7 lakh schools, 24.7 crore students, and 1 crore teachers. Rural enrolment among children aged 6-14 has reached 98%, while literacy among those aged seven and above stands at 81%.But the next challenge is ensuring children actually learn. The Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) 2024 shows that among Class III students in govt schools, the proportion able to read a Class II-level text improved from 16.3% in 2022 to 23.4% in 2024, while those able to solve subtraction rose from 20.2% to 27.6%.The gains are encouraging but also underline the distance still to be covered.Govt initiatives such as NIPUN Bharat, Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI and DIKSHA are attempting to address this challenge through foundational literacy, teacher training, digital learning and school infrastructure. Yet the scale of the task means govts alone cannot do everything. That is where CSR is beginning to play a more strategic role.Education has emerged as the single largest recipient of CSR funding in India. According to the latest CSRBOX report, India Inc spent Rs 40,794 crore on CSR during FY2024-25 across more than 72,000 projects. Education accounted for Rs 13,877 crore, or 34% of the total, making it the country’s biggest CSR sector. More significantly, companies are moving away from one-off philanthropy towards multi-year programmes, govt partnerships and data-driven monitoring of outcomes.Bharti Airtel Foundation offers one example of this transition. During FY2024-25, the foundation reported reaching more than 22 lakh students across over 16,000 schools. Its cumulative programmes have impacted 3.7 million students, more than 36,000 schools, and over 3.3 lakh teachers.Rather than focusing solely on infrastructure, its initiatives include teacher support, school transformation, life skills, and community engagement. Its Satya Bharti School Programme operates 164 rural schools across four states, while its Quality Support Programme works with govt schools in 12 states.Another example is Tata STRIVE, which reflects the growing emphasis on employability. In FY2024-25, it directly reached over 4.5 lakh young people and reported cumulative outreach of more than 22.5 lakh beneficiaries through skill development, career guidance, vocational education and entrepreneurship programmes. The focus extends beyond classrooms to ensuring education translates into livelihoods and economic participation.This evolution mirrors the changing needs of India’s education system. While access has improved dramatically, important gaps remain. Nearly 8% of 15-16-year-olds are no longer enrolled in school, with girls recording slightly higher non-enrolment than boys.Infrastructure has also improved unevenly. Although over 99% of schools have drinking water and nearly 94% have electricity, only about two-thirds have computers and internet access, while just 35.6% have dedicated toilets for children with special needs.These are challenges that require sustained investment rather than isolated interventions. Increasingly, CSR is being used not to substitute public spending but to complement it by piloting new models, supporting teachers, strengthening school systems and helping govts scale successful practices.India has already built one of the world’s largest education systems. The next phase is about making that scale deliver better outcomes. Public investment will remain the foundation, but if current trends continue, CSR could become an important catalyst in helping schools move from expanding access to improving learning, ensuring that every rupee invested delivers lasting change for students, teachers and communities.
Article Summary: India has largely succeeded in getting children into school. Rural enrolment among children aged 6-14 has reached 98%. But the next challenge is ensuring children actually learn. Education has emerged as the single largest recipient of CSR funding in India.

Article Title: 'No blanket ban on reporting': SC clarifies order restricting use of audio-video clips of court proceedings

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has clarified that its July 24 interim order prohibiting news organisations from sharing or uploading audio and video clips of court hearings does not bar them from reporting on judicial proceedings, but that they cannot use such recordings as part of their reportage.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the restriction is confined to the use of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings in news reports and should not be interpreted as a blanket ban on reportage by media organisations. Such outlets may, therefore, continue to report on the proceedings and inform the general public of legal developments and judicial pronouncements."It appears, however, that some confusion persists in respect of paragraph 11 of the earlier order, which this court deems necessary to clarify. The said paragraph makes it clear that the order is not to be construed as imposing a blanket prohibition on the reporting of court proceedings by recognised news outlets," the bench said in an order on July 31, PTI reported.However, the news organisations will have to follow the restrictions set out in paragraph 10 of the earlier order."In sum, while news outlets may continue to report on the court proceedings, they shall nonetheless remain bound by the restrictions set out in paragraph 10,” the bench added.The clarification came after Supreme Court noted that "some confusion persists" over the interim order, which barred posting and uploading of audio-video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms without prior permission of the court administration.“As an interim measure, it is directed that there shall be no extraction, modification, dissemination, monetisation, posting, reposting and uploading of audio-video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media or other digital platforms without prior permission of the secretary general of this court or the registrar general of the jurisdictional high courts,” the bench had stated in that order.The Supreme Court had also issued notices to the Centre and others, including some social media platforms, seeking their responses on the plea filed by a journalist.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, had described the issue raised in the petition as "very important."
Article Summary: Supreme Court clarifies interim order for new sorganisations on audio-video clips of court proceedings. The restriction is confined to the use of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings in news reports. The clarification came after Supreme Court noted that "some confusion persists" over the interim order.

NEW DELHI: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has taken up the issue of alleged advertisements linked to child sexual exploitative and abuse material (CSAM) with Meta and has instituted an inquiry to determine the facts of the matter.Persons in the know said NCPCR had taken note of a media report that alleged the presence of advertisements related to CSAM on the company's platforms. The the child rights body sought an explanation from Meta regarding the allegations and the company submitted its response about a week later.After examining the reply, the panel has now decided to institute a formal inquiry into the matter to ascertain the facts and examine the issues raised in the media report.The development comes amid heightened scrutiny of online platforms over child safety. Authorities have increasingly been pressing social media and digital platforms to strengthen safeguards, improve content moderation systems and ensure compliance with Indian laws aimed at protecting children online.
Article Summary: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has taken up the issue of alleged advertisements linked to child sexual exploitative and abuse material (CSAM) with Meta. NCPCR has instituted an inquiry to determine the facts of the matter.
